text:
sam: Heads-up — spotted a perf regression when selector falls back to Triton on SM90 for paged-attn. Backend falls back at ~seq=2048 and latency jumps ~2.3x compared to CUDA path.
anya: ugh, reproducible locally?
sam: yes on devbox (A100-SM80 emulator) and on a SM90 instance. Quick numbers:
```
CUDA path (flashx): p50=48ms p95=72ms
Triton fallback: p50=110ms p95=180ms
workload: seq=2048, batch=4, kv-pages=8
```
matt: do we see different behavior across CUDA versions? Triton pinned?
kevin: runs on CUDA 12.2 + Triton 2.2.5 here. The selector logic uses per-arch heuristic: if sm>=90 and seq>1024 choose flashx, else triton? maybe bug in threshold calc.
sam: selector logs show it picks Triton because it mis-evaluates `supports_pagedfusion=true` but `vectorized_kv=false` for this model.
perf-bot: nightly bench: https://ci/reports/1998765400 — flagged +130% p50 for paged-attn on sm90-triton combo :rotating_light:
anya: can you paste the selector debug for the request?
sam: sure:
```
[selector] model=redwood/v1/paged-attn variant=fp16
arch=sm90 cuda=12.2 triton=2.2.5
heuristics: max_seq=4096, kv_pages=8, batch=4
capabilities: flashx=True, paged_fusion=True, paged_kv_vectorized=False
decision: fallback_to_triton=true (reason: paged_kv_vectorized==false)
```
kevin: that last flag should be true for our compiled runtime on SM90. Looks like the kernel capability probe returned false. Could be a build mismark or runtime symbol mismatch.
matt: also check kv warmup behavior — if KV pages are cold, Triton kernel does extra memcpy which blows up latency. Was cache warm?
sam: warm runs still bad but slightly better: p50 down to 95ms. So warmup helps but not enough.
anya: next steps: 1) capture profiler traces for both paths (cuda & triton) 2) run selector unit test to reproduce capability mismatch 3) try forced-flashx run to confirm perf.
kevin: assigning to infra team to run `ldd`/symbol check on runtime binary used in SM90 image. I'll try to reproduce with the exact image.
perf-bot: attaching perf traces: s3://perf/traces/1998765432_flashx.trace and s3://perf/traces/1998765432_triton.trace
sam: quick diff from traces: Triton path shows a lot of `memcpyAsync` stalls and kernel launch serialization. CUDA path shows contiguous fused kernel with small kernel durations.
matt: hypothesis: Triton kernels compiled for cuda12.1 have a scheduling inefficiency on sm90 that multiplies kernel latency for large sequence lengths. Also selector bug flips due to missing vectorized_kv flag.
anya: can we add a temporary guard: if arch==sm90 && seq>1536 prefer flashx even if vectorized_kv==false? Just to triage.
kevin: yes can push a canary change to selector with that guard and a metric to watch. Will open a PR and deploy to canary cluster.
sam: i'll run microbench harness with forced flashx/tuned batching heuristics: try lowering batch->2, increase pv pages to 12 to see effect.
anya: also add a regression test into the selector tests that covers sm90+cuda12.2+tĭton (simulate).
matt: FYI: if this turns out to be a Triton kernel bug we should add fallback to our CUDA compiled kernels instead of Triton for sm90.
kevin: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721 — selector guard + metric. Deploying to canary now.
perf-bot: canary results (first hour): no user-facing errors, p50 improved from 110ms -> 52ms on canary nodes (forced flashx guard).
sam: great. keeping this thread for follow-ups: need root cause on capability probe + long-term fix in triton kernels or force cuda builds.
anya: assigning follow-ups: kevin (probe/build mismatch), matt (Triton perf investigation), sam (bench matrix + KV warmup experiments).
kevin: noted, I'll post updates here. :thumbsup:
matt: I'll try to reproduce on local SM90 dev rig and instrument kernel timelines.
sam: thanks all, moving off slack to create an issue with artifacts and steps.
kevin: leaving logs here for the issue: `nvprof --profile-from-start off --trace-memcpy yes` and the selector debug mode.
perf-bot: closing loop: will run longer 24h canary and report regressions.
